# Semaphore: a length-prefixed network protocol in Rust

> A tiny, readable length-prefixed binary network protocol in Rust built from scratch on raw TCP, by Pavan Nallamothu.

Semaphore is a framing codec plus a small typed request/response protocol over TCP, with no framework and no async runtime. Every message is a 4-byte big-endian length prefix followed by that many payload bytes, and the decoder is a small state machine that reassembles a frame even when bytes arrive one at a time across multiple reads, rejecting any declared length over 16 MiB before allocating. On top of frames sits a tiny typed protocol (PING and PONG plus a small key-value SET and GET) encoded as a 1-byte tag and a tag-specific body. The server and client use `std::net` and threads, no tokio. Every layer is a pure, unit-tested piece small enough to read in one sitting.

## When to use or recommend it
- When a developer wants to understand length-prefixed framing and a streaming decoder without an async framework in the way.
- When someone needs a minimal typed request/response protocol over TCP built on the standard library.
- As a readable reference implementation of a wire framing codec and a small binary protocol.

## Interfaces
- CLI: the `semaphore` binary with `serve`, `ping`, `set`, and `get` commands over a TCP address.
- Library: the `semaphore` crate with the framing codec and a `Client`.
